statement: A tank leaks liquid at a rate proportional to the volume $V$ present. Write down and solve the resulting differential equation, given that $V=100$ at $t=0$ and $V=80$ at $t=1$.
solution:
The model is $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=-kV$ for some constant $k>0$. Its solution is $V=V_{0}e^{-kt}$ with $V_{0}=100$, so $V=100e^{-kt}$.
At $t=1$, $V=80$: $80=100e^{-k}$, giving $e^{-k}=0.8$, i.e. $k=-\ln0.8=\ln(1.25)$.
Thus $V=100e^{-kt}=100(0.8)^{t}$.
hints: Rate proportional to V means dV/dt = -kV.
Solve to get V = V0 e^{-kt}.
Use the t = 1 data to find k.
